title: Measurement: Length, Mass, Volume, Temperature and Time
summary: Measuring and converting units of length, mass, volume and temperature, working with time and timetables, and calculating perimeter and area in practical contexts.

notes.label: Remember
notes.text: Going to a **smaller** unit, **multiply** (2,5 m = 250 cm). Going to a **larger** unit, **divide** (750 g = 0,75 kg).

notes.caption: Converting between degrees Celsius and Fahrenheit

notes.title: Worked example 1
notes.problem: An oven recipe says 350 °F. What is this in °C?

items: 60 seconds = 1 minute; 60 minutes = 1 hour; 24 hours = 1 day.
To find elapsed time, count hours and minutes separately, e.g. 08:50 to 13:15 is 4 h 25 min.

notes.title: Worked example 2: a bus timetable
notes.problem: A bus leaves Pretoria at 07:40 and arrives in Polokwane at 11:05. How long is the trip?

notes.title: Worked example 3: tiling a floor
notes.problem: A rectangular floor is 4,2 m by 3,5 m. Tiles are sold in boxes covering 1,44 m² each, at R289 per box. Allow 10% extra for breakages. What will the tiles cost?

notes.label: Exam tip
notes.text: Always round **up** when buying materials (boxes, tins of paint, rolls), because shops sell whole units and you must have enough.

questions.prompt: How many 250 mℓ glasses can be filled from a 2 ℓ bottle?
A shift starts at 06:45 and ends at 15:15. How long is the shift?
A rectangular garden is 12 m long and 7,5 m wide. How many metres of fencing are needed to go around it?
Calculate the area of a circular table top with radius 0,6 m (use $\pi = 3{,}142$), to two decimal places.
A wall is 5 m long and 2,7 m high, with a window of 1,2 m by 1 m. One litre of paint covers 8 m², and paint is sold in 2 ℓ tins. How many tins are needed for two coats?
questions.memo:
✓ Wall area 13,5 m² − 1,2 m² = 12,3 m² (1)
✓ Two coats: 24,6 m² (1)
✓ Paint: 24,6 ÷ 8 = 3,075 ℓ (1)
✓ 2 tins (4 ℓ) (1)
